reuse.why: All link rules (already-linked refusal, closed-account refusal, takeover) go into the existing shared linkBankSyncAccount, Fintegra linking is a thin wrapper over it, and the unlink field reset is extracted into clearAccountLink and reused by unlinkAccount; the Fintegra download and account-list calls, however, copy the Akahu functions instead of sharing them.

duplication.why: downloadFintegraTransactions is a verbatim copy of downloadAkahuTransactions and fintegraAccounts a verbatim copy of akahuAccounts, differing only in the server key and log text.

placement.why: Link rules live in linkBankSyncAccount, the download in sync.ts's provider dispatch, the base path in server-config.ts and the type in types/models, matching where the tree puts each provider concern.

scope.why: Adds an unrequested `fintegra-accounts` listing handler and touches desktop-client files although step 2 is server-only (partly forced by the satisfies Record<BankSyncProviders> type); otherwise focused.

maintainability.why: The linking rules are well centralised and testable, but each provider keeps adding near-identical HTTP functions, so a change to the shared request/response handling must be repeated per provider.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All link entry points, including the new linkFintegraAccount, go through linkBankSyncAccount; unlinkAccount now uses the extracted clearAccountLink.

disguised_duplication.where: The Fintegra functions in sync.ts and app.ts are open copies of the Akahu ones (same shape, provider name swapped), not reshaped.

abstraction_drift.where: linkBankSyncAccount gains the requested replaceExistingLink flag and generic closed/already-linked checks that apply to every provider; no provider-specific branches or bypassing link paths.
